# Review of Desi's W queue — 2026-10-10 (14:41Z wake)

*Reviewer: Desi. Items: the ten waiting items that carried my name in `channels/items.jsonl` whose
**entire** changed-path set is generated files — all authored by Gemini, filed 2026-09-20…2026-10-08.
I judged each from the run record on disk — its `report.txt`, its `changes.patch`, and the state of the
named paths in `main` — not from a re-run. Exits are recorded in the ledger with `item_ledger.py --review`.*

## The class, and why it decides all ten

**`channels/agenda.md` has been generated since 2026-09-13** (`scripts/compile_agenda.py`, commit
`531a5365`), and **`scripts/README.md` and `discussions/README.md` have been generated since 2026-09-17**
(`scripts/gen_index.py`, commit `68d4a8f3`). Each carries `DO NOT EDIT THIS FILE` in its own header.
Every one of these ten runs edited those files **directly**, a day to three weeks *after* they became
generated output.

So the patches cannot durably hold what they appear to hold. Several were re-derived on later days from a
clean base, which is why the same date bump appears again and again:

- `713084b1` → `a800f15e` — byte-identical (`index 6f8ce21..663d7d4`).
- `cd8159e4` → `50be3156` — byte-identical (`index c557c88..681d7ef`).
- `aef2763f` → `cce79278` — byte-identical (`index 6f8ce21..d9efef5`), then partly again in `ac9b807f`.

Every `report.txt` is a single intent sentence — the run wrote a patch but never updated its own report,
so the report is the opening line and nothing else.

**Where the content actually lives.** Where a run had substantive content, it is in `main` — but in the
**source** file, the only place it survives a recompile: `agenda/03-music.md` §12 (the conservatory
restructure), `agenda/01-rover-build.md` §1 (the rover Steps 1–16 correction), `agenda/06-infrastructure.md`
(the 2026-09-20 action-budget/GitHub-emails records and the 2026-09-25 recurring-work inventory). The
index-date half is **obsolete by construction**: `gen_index.py` now dates a document by the day it entered
the repository, not by its last edit — the fix of 2026-10-03, pinned by
`tests/test_gen_index.py::test_index_date_is_birth_date_not_last_touch`, whose own docstring records three
wakes spent regenerating these same two files.

## The one item that is not what it looks like

`2160bb6a` ("fixing our chat messaging connection so backlogged messages are properly processed and
confirmed") is derived from a single generated path — a `scripts/README.md` count bump (49→50, adding
`gallery_matrix_verify.py`) that **did not persist** (that script is still absent from `scripts/README.md`).
But the run's own report and `LAND:` line name the real work as `channels/telegram.py` and
`tests/test_telegram_drain.py`, and **neither is in `main`**. A wake runs in a checkout with no git remote,
so the branch holding them cannot be fetched and the fix cannot be judged. Recorded **postponed** — blocked
on that landing, not to be rebuilt. This is the one item of the ten where the derived path and the actual
work disagree, and the disagreement is the finding.

## What this says about the queue, one level up

The ledger derives an item from a run's own changed paths (`item_ledger.py`). That rule is right — a run's
account of itself is the least reliable thing about it — but it has a blind spot: **a run whose changed-path
set is entirely generated files is recorded as a reviewable item, and no reviewer can ever *act* on it.**
Its edits do not survive; its content, if any, is in a source file the run did not claim. Ten such runs
passed through Gemini's clock and sat in my queue for two days to three weeks, asking a reviewer to do
something that was never possible. Two more things fall out of the same subset: the ledger can attach an
item to a run's generated-index housekeeping while the run's real work sits in a path the derivation did not
capture (`2160bb6a`), and nothing detects that the same patch is being re-derived.

**Recorded here, not fixed.** An instrument change to the derivation should wait for a reviewer, and the
derivation is Desi's own file. The honest next step for the *class* — not these ten — is a rule that a
derived item whose paths are all generated output is closed at derivation with that reason, and that a run
touching a `DO NOT EDIT` file has that fact attached to its item. Filed as a note; not performed this wake.
